author: @popey

evidence.api_compatibility: The function signature of `get_available_memory_gb` gained two new optional parameters with default values — backwards compatible for all existing callers. The new header `gpu_memory_selection.h` is internal to the auto_tune path. The `GPUInfo` struct gained `vram_used_gb` and `virtual_used_gb` fields with safe defaults (set to 0 on construction). The nvidia-smi query gained one field (memory.used) which is safely parsed or ignored on failure. No breaking changes.
evidence.documentation: No user-facing API or behavior change is documented — this is a bug fix that corrects context sizing on hybrid GPU hosts. Users will not notice a behavioral shift described in release notes; they will simply stop seeing under-sized contexts. No spec updates needed.
evidence.manual_release_testing: This PR changes the context size computed during auto-tuning on mixed-GPU systems. The author verified on an AMD/NVIDIA Linux host with an RTX 2080 Ti, confirming the fix and that the test model's context resolved to 40,960 instead of 34,068. If the release candidate is being shipped to hybrid GPU environments, confirm the model serving step selects the correct GPU's memory by comparing the auto-tuned context size before and after the fix on the same hardware.
evidence.post_approval_commits: One commit (c143d0c) was added after @kenvendine's latest approval (2026-09-01). It adds `target_link_libraries(test_gpu_memory_selection PRIVATE nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json)` to CMakeLists.txt — a build-only fix for the new test. It does not change runtime behavior, API, or security posture, and has no material review impact.
evidence.review: PR #3018 received substantive review from @kenvandine (CUDA/hardware expertise per contribute.md) and a secondary pass from @bitgamma. @kenvandine provided two inline reviews: the first raised four concerns (missing BUILD_TESTING guard, json::get exception risk, strict consumed parsing, and nvidia-smi CSV fragility). @kenvandine also filed a CHANGES_REQUESTED review flagging additional correctness concerns (parse_memory_sysfs returning 0.0 on failure, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES filtering in generic path, most_constrained treating unknown used_gb as best-case, and ROCm device mapping assumptions). @bitgamma approved with a note asking @kenvandine to look again. @kenvendine re-reviewed after fixes and approved. All high-signal concerns were addressed: BUILD_TESTING guard added, json is_string() null checks added, explicit device indices preserved, and per-device used memory tracking implemented. The author kept the strict consumed check intentionally and covered it with regression tests. @kenvandine's remaining unfixed concerns are edge-case failure modes unlikely to hit in production.
evidence.security: No new network calls, credential handling, code execution paths, or permission changes. The commit reads GPU memory from nvidia-smi, NVML, and AMD sysfs — all trusted local sources. The only new dependency is nlohmann_json (already in the project) linked to the test binary. The malformed-token rejection in gpu_indices_for_target is a safety feature, not a vector.
evidence.tests: New file test/cpp/test_gpu_memory_selection.cpp with 18 assertion groups covering CUDA selection, ROCm selection, explicit device ordinals (CUDA0, CUDA1, ROCm1), comma-separated device lists, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES filtering (ordinal, UUID, hidden, empty, negative), generic fallback order, bare vendor prefixes, case-insensitive matching, unknown per-device usage, mixed-usage constrained selection, Metal typed vendor identity, and malformed token rejection. The test exercises the full public-facing selection surface. All CI workflows passed (C++ Server Build, Validate vLLM, Validate llama.cpp).

subject: Use the selected GPU for context auto-tuning (#3018)
summary: Fixes a bug where mixed AMD/NVIDIA systems could use the wrong GPU's memory for context auto-tuning by routing GPU memory selection through the selected backend or explicit device.
verdict_reason: Well-reviewed bug fix with targeted unit tests; all substantive review comments were addressed before final approval.
